Apple is set to unveil its new iPhones next week, and a Bloomberg report today details the specifications of these new models as well as the product roadmap for 2027 and 2028.

Apple is reportedly preparing to launch more than 10 new iPhone models by 2028—here are the details.

Ahead of Apple's big September event next week, Mark Gurman published an overview today of this fall's and future new products. He detailed hardware still in the pipeline through 2028.

Here's Gurman's rundown of the new iPhones expected to launch:

2026: Unveiling at the September 9 Event Next Week

  • iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: Featuring a mechanical aperture lens function, available in deep red and light blue, powered by the A20 Pro chip and C2 modem, with improved battery life, among other upgrades.
  • iPhone Ultra: A foldable model "roughly the size of a passport when folded," available in light and dark colour options, equipped with Touch ID and an "advanced hinge," priced at over US$2,000.

2027

  • iPhone 18 and 18e: No specific details provided apart from a "spring" launch window; the base iPhone 18 will be removed from the fall lineup.
  • iPhone Air 2: Three key upgrades: an ultrawide camera, a faster chip, and longer battery life.
  • iPhone Pro and Pro Max Models: A distinctive 20th-anniversary design will feature "curved glass on all four sides and edges, with narrower bezels." According to Gurman: "This will be the most significant redesign of the iPhone Pro lineup since the iPhone X."
  • Second-generation Foldable iPhone: The new foldable model "has entered advanced testing stages." The only new feature mentioned is a new chip.

2028

  • Larger-screen Foldable iPhone: A third-generation foldable is in development, with "slightly larger front and internal displays" compared to the 2026 and 2027 models.

Gurman did not provide details on other 2028 models. However, new base models and Pro models are expected. The larger screens on the third-generation foldable are worth noting, as market trends show consumers continuing to demand bigger displays.

Which new iPhone on Apple's roadmap interests you the most? Let us know in the comments.
